rows.reasoning: The only record on file is SB 1057 (2026), which Finchem prime-sponsored and voted Y on: it repeals and replaces A.R.S. 16-504 to require that ballot paper carry vendor-certified "Ballot fraud countermeasures" such as watermarks, holographic foil and security inks. That regulates the ballot itself, not how the government verifies a voter, so it does not touch the clauses that separate "Require no identification to vote, verifying voters by signature or existing records" from "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote" (annex hard case: ballots, not voters). No passage survives V2, so no chair is evidenced.
